chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Divorce is not valid under compulsion, nor is emancipation valid under compulsion, nor is an oath valid for cutting off kinship, nor for anything from the disobedience of Allah. So whoever swears or is made to swear regarding any of this, and he acts upon it, there is nothing upon him (no expiation is required).'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rather, the divorce is that which is intended by it without compulsion, and without harm to the waiting period, and the Sunnah is upon purity (from menses) without sexual intercourse, and with two witnesses. So whoever opposes this, then neither his divorce nor his oath is valid, and it is returned to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.الطُّهْرُ: Purity (specifically from menses in this context)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce in Shia Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential criteria for the validity of divorce (talaq) and emancipation (itq), asserting that compulsion (istikrah) invalidates these acts unless the intent is preserved. It further clarifies that oaths taken for minor sins or under duress do not require expiation (kaffarah), while establishing the Sunnah protocol for divorce during a period of purity free from intercourse and witnessed by two individuals. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on voluntary intent and procedural correctness to ensure the divorce is legally binding and returns to the Quranic framework.
